7|## Trek to the Prison
8|
9|Varrin has sent word to his agents, and Bethra (chaotic good, dwarf [spy](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17021-spy)) meets the characters when they arrive in Luskan. She provides the uniforms for their chosen cover and directs them to report to a ship called the Jolly Pelican the following dawn. The ship regularly delivers a fresh rotation of prison staff to Revel’s End and returns the relieved shift to the Sword Coast. The journey to Revel’s End by sea is 350 miles, which a sailing ship can cover in three days under normal conditions.
10|
11|Twenty-five guards and six cooks are bound for the prison, including any characters taking their places. If the characters express concern over the fate of staff they’re replacing, Bethra assures them that none of the people were killed, and they’ll be released safely when the job is over.
12|
13|The players can make up whatever names they like for their cover. Those are the names of the guards or cooks they’ve replaced.
```
</user_selected_content>

9|Varrin has sent word to his agents, and Bethra, a chaotic good dwarf [[spy]], meets the characters in [[Stickyickistan]]. She provides uniforms, badges, and forged transfer orders for the characters' chosen cover identities. They are replacing members of the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition|THC]] detail assigned to escort [[Unit BH-Umbra Δ9]] aboard [[The Recluse]]. Bethra directs them to report to the THC staging area before the airship's scheduled departure.
10|
11|The Recluse is preparing to carry the prisoners north to [[Giantfrost Penitentiary]]. The flight will take several days, giving the Heist Squad time to establish their covers, learn the ship's security procedures, and identify the best opportunity to help the Raven squad seize the vessel. The characters should be told that their real allies will not reveal themselves until the operation is underway.
12|
13|Twenty-five guards and six cooks are assigned to The Recluse, including any characters taking the guards' places. The cooks are not part of the formal security detail, but they have access to the crew areas, kitchens, stores, and service passages. If the characters express concern over the fate of the staff they’re replacing, Bethra assures them that the people were not killed and will be released safely once the extraction is complete.
14|
15|The players can make up whatever names they like for their cover identities. Those are the names of the THC guards or ship staff they have replaced. Bethra warns them that senior officers may know the original staff by sight, so the characters should avoid drawing attention to themselves until they have learned enough about their assumed identities.
```
</user_selected_content>

73|### 4. The Cook’s Emergency
74|
75|A cook assigned to The Recluse discovers that one of the food stores has been contaminated with a strange alchemical substance. The substance is not immediately lethal, but it causes hallucinations, nausea, or temporary paralysis.
76|
77|The THC assumes this is an assassination attempt against the prisoners and orders the entire kitchen staff detained. The characters must investigate the contamination without exposing their true mission.
78|
79|Possible explanations include:
80|
81|- A careless alchemical storage mistake
82|- Sabotage by someone trying to delay the departure
83|- A substance placed by an agent of the Ashen Shadow Society
84|- An escaped creature hiding in the food stores
85|- A failed attempt to drug the guards
86|
87|The characters can gain access to restricted service passages, identify the substance, protect the cooks, and potentially turn the incident into a useful distraction.
88|
89|---
90|
91|### 5. The Guard Who Wants to Do the Right Thing
92|
93|A young THC guard approaches one of the characters privately. They have heard rumours that [[Unit BH-Umbra Δ9]] is being sent away without a proper appeal and believe the prisoners may have been treated unfairly.
94|
95|The guard does not know the characters are infiltrators. They simply want reassurance that they are not helping disappear innocent people.
96|
97|The characters must decide how much of the truth to reveal. They could:
98|
99|- Convince the guard that the prisoners are dangerous
100|- Encourage the guard to look the other way later
101|- Recruit them as an inside ally
102|- Feed them a false explanation
103|- Tell them enough truth to gain their trust
104|
105|If recruited, the guard can provide a believable reason for the characters to access restricted areas or can delay the alarm when the Raven squad begins the assault. If betrayed or intimidated, the guard becomes a source of suspicion during the flight.
```
</user_selected_content>

119|## Halfling Overboard
120|
121|It wasn’t long before the Strider Airship, _Recluse_, having departed the dwarven city of Soldorakhold only the day before, was beset by a group of human pirates aboard a pair of Lyrandar Skyskiffs as they passed over the vast Ironroot Mountains. See [chapter 7](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota/elemental-airships) of _[Eberron: Forge of the Artificer](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota)_ for the [Strider Airship](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota/elemental-airships#StriderAirship) and [Lyrandar Skyskiff](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota/elemental-airships#LyrandarSkyskiff) statistics.
122|
123|Eight pirates boarded the _Recluse_ when the _Recluse’s_ captain, a halfling named Ryvan Rallanith, made a brash decision; he veered the ship into a steep dive. Four of the pirates fell overboard—however, not before one of them cut the harnesses lashing Captain Rallanith to the helm. Four pirates remain aboard the airship.
124|
125|The soarwood planks of the ship groan and creak in protest as the Recluse hangs helplessly in the sky, the bow pitching steeply. Thousands of galifars’ worth of unsecured supplies and, more importantly, the halfling captain Ryvan Rallanith, are now black specks fading away hundreds of feet beneath.
126|
127|Kreffik Soldorak, your employer, lies in a heap of furniture and luggage nearby. “Dolurrh!” he cries out, pushing a small nightstand off himself and attempting to straighten out his coat, “what is that thrice-damned helmsman doing?!”
128|
129|Without a pilot, there’s no chance of the ship righting itself, let alone continuing their voyage.
```
</user_selected_content>

```content/Adventures/DM Notes/Intercepting the Recluse.md
119|## The Raven Squad Is Cast Off
120|
121|Several hours into the flight, once the Heist Squad has had time to establish its cover and learn the THC’s procedures, the Raven squad arrives aboard its Society-owned airship. It rises from below The Recluse and draws alongside, allowing the Raven operatives to cross over by grappling lines. Their arrival is sudden and controlled. The THC guards have little time to understand what is happening before the Raven squad reaches the flight deck and confronts the captain.
122|
123|The Raven squad’s orders are to seize control of The Recluse long enough for the Heist Squad to release [[Unit BH-Umbra Δ9]]. The captain, however, reacts before they can secure him. Rather than allow the vessel to be taken, he throws The Recluse into a steep dive. The ship pitches violently, sending unsecured equipment, supplies, and personnel sliding across the deck.
124|
125|At the last moment, the captain cuts the harness lashing him to the helm. The sudden movement and severed restraints send the Raven squad tumbling away from The Recluse. Their operatives disappear into the clouds below, along with the chance for the Heist Squad to rely on outside support. The Society airship is forced to pull away and search for the fallen squad, leaving the Heist Squad behind aboard The Recluse.
126|
127|The ship groans as it struggles to recover from the dive. The captain is no longer at the helm, the Raven squad is gone, and the THC detail is beginning to regain control of itself. The Heist Squad must now finish the extraction alone. They need to reach the security office, bypass the protections on the prisoner compartment, release [[Unit BH-Umbra Δ9]], and regain control of The Recluse before the THC can identify them as infiltrators.
128|
129|The characters have only a short time before the surviving THC officers organize a response. If they act quickly, they can use the confusion to reach the prisoners and redirect The Recluse toward a rendezvous with the Society’s airship. If they delay, the guards seal the prisoner compartment, move the prisoners to a secondary holding area, and begin searching the ship for the intruders who helped the Raven squad board.
130|
131|The Raven squad’s disappearance should not end the adventure. It removes the characters’ planned support and forces them to rely on the information, alliances, and access they gained while undercover. The extraction is still possible, but from this point forward, the Heist Squad is on its own.
```
</user_selected_content>

```content/Adventures/DM Notes/Intercepting the Recluse.md
130|### Regaining Control of the Helm
131|
132|A creature occupying the Helm crew station of an airship typically requires the [Mark of the Storm](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/ffotr/fated-flight-of-the-recluse) to access the station’s actions (see [chapter 7](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota/elemental-airships/#Chapter7ElementalAirships) of _[Eberron: Forge of the Artificer](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota)_ for more on crew stations). The _Recluse_, however, is unique in that the airship is powered not only by a captive [air elemental](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194878-air-elemental), but also the spirit of a long-dead previous captain who, having fallen into the elemental ring, was absorbed into the airship’s elemental core. The spirit’s inhabitancy allows a creature occupying the Helm to bypass that station’s requirements and use the station’s actions regardless.
133|
134|A character that takes the [Study](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#StudyAction) action and succeeds on a DC 9 Intelligence ([Arcana](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#Skills)) check recalls not only that a pilot must bear a Mark of the Storm, but also that [House Lyrandar](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/ffotr/fated-flight-of-the-recluse) tightly controls individuals bearing such a mark; given that the former pilot wasn’t a member of House Lyrandar, it’s more likely than not that the ship can be controlled by someone without the dragonmark, and that Captain Rallanith deduced another way to do so.
135|
136|The ship is currently tilted steeply enough that the airship’s vertical surfaces are horizontal to the ground. The characters’ options now depend on where they were when Captain Rallanith entered the dive. Give the players a few minutes to describe their characters and what they were doing prior to their being attacked by pirates.
137|
138|_**On the Deck.**_ While Captain Rallanith shouted for the characters to take shelter within the _Recluse’s_ interior, those that might have ignored the order were hastily issued harnesses and now find themselves lashed to a safety rail that runs along the airship’s gunwale.
139|
140|_**Inside the Airship.**_ Those that heeded the captain’s orders are in a room of their choosing within the airship’s interior.
141|
142|#### [](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/ffotr/fated-flight-of-the-recluse#ReachingtheHelm)Reaching the Helm
143|
144|With Captain Rallanith’s demise, the ship’s Helm is unoccupied. A character that wishes to right the airship must first reach and interface with the Helm.
145|
146|**_Inside the Airship._** Due to the ship’s tilted orientation, creatures inside the ship must climb to access other areas of the ship. A creature without a Climb Speed that attempts to climb inside the ship must succeed on a DC 11 Strength ([Athletics](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#Skills)) check or fall.
147|
148|**_On the Deck._** Creatures wearing harnesses on the ship’s deck can climb the deck’s vertical surface without falling. A creature has [Disadvantage](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#Disadvantage) on attack rolls while wearing a harness.
149|
150|As a [Utilize](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#UtilizeAction) action, a creature can make a DC 11 Strength ([Athletics](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#Skills)) check to remove the harness, safely doing so without falling on a successful check. When a creature without a harness is pushed or gains the [Prone](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#ProneCondition) condition, the creature must succeed on a DC 11 Dexterity saving throw or fall—potentially off the ship and to its death.
151|
152|#### [](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/ffotr/fated-flight-of-the-recluse#Pirates)Pirates
153|
154|Four pirates (Medium [Bandit Captains](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/5194912-bandit-captain)) aboard the _Recluse_, also wearing harnesses, engage the characters. The pirates remaining aboard their own skyskiffs continue their attempts to capture the _Recluse_. Each skyskiff is 30 feet away from the _Recluse_, has harpooned the airship using the [Tow Cable](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota/elemental-airships#TowCable) crew station, and is slowly dragging it toward their base of operations in the Ironroot Mountains. Each of the two skyskiffs has one pirate (Medium **Bandit Captain**) remaining aboard.
155|
156|#### [](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/ffotr/fated-flight-of-the-recluse#GhostintheMachine)Ghost in the Machine
157|
158|A character attempting to operate the Helm (see _[Eberron: Forge of the Artificer](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota)_, [chapter 7](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/efota/elemental-airships/#OperatinganAirship)) notices an unusual telepathic presence that reaches out to them when they touch it. The presence (described in the “[Captain Valthan d’Lyrandar](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/ffotr/fated-flight-of-the-recluse#CaptainValthandLyrandar)” sidebar) is initially [Indifferent](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#IndifferentAttitude) to the character.
159|
160|A character that takes the [Influence](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#InfluenceAction) action and succeeds on a DC 17 Charisma ([Deception](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#Skills), [Intimidation](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#Skills), or [Persuasion](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/playing-the-game#Skills)) check changes the presence’s attitude to [Friendly](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#FriendlyAttitude) and convinces it to allow them to access the Helm’s actions. Characters that have proficiency with Navigator’s Tools make this check with [Advantage](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#Advantage), while characters with the [Mark of Storm](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/ffotr/fated-flight-of-the-recluse) automatically succeed on this check. The presence’s attitude changes to [Hostile](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#HostileAttitude) if the check fails by 5 or more.
```
</user_selected_content>
